findings.reason: a node following the deliverable reaches a gate its own assets cannot pass, and can only get green by lowering the threshold for these routes (changing §13's behaviour, which §17 does not authorise) or by pointing `RECKON_UI_ROOT` (`reckon/serve.py:547`) at a large fixture asset tree the plan never names.
findings.text: "Compiled scripts and runtimes are gzipped above §13's threshold" is inert at the threshold it names: `_GZIP_MIN_BYTES` is 64 KiB per file (`reckon/serve.py:179`), and of the 34 script-and-stylesheet tags the served shell links (`docs/index.html`) exactly one exceeds it — `/_runtime/react-dom.js` at 131,835 B; the largest compiled script, `/_ui/plan.js`, is 63,662 B and every other compiled script is smaller, so the clause compresses a single runtime while the done-when's "a compiled script … answers `Content-Encoding: gzip`" (plan.html:282) has no real compiled script that can satisfy it

findings.reason: the discrepancy is marginal for this node — the section's substantive claim, that the scripts are served `no-store` and uncompressed through `_send` on every load, is verified in the code (`reckon/serve.py:2848-2905` routes `/_runtime/*.js` and compiled `/_ui/*.js` through `_send`, whose fallback header is `Cache-Control: no-store`), and no gate in §17 or §11 turns on the exact byte total — but the figure should cite its own measurement rather than §11's pass, which does not carry it.
findings.text: the byte figures "719,562 B, or 190,459 B gzipped" do not reproduce: measured at the reviewed head over the shell's own 34 linked tags, using the server's `compile_jsx`/`client_runtime_assets` for compiled and runtime assets and `gzip.compress(level=5)` as `_send_file` uses, the set totals 784,186 B raw and 203,941 B gzipped (about 8 % above each stated figure), and neither number appears in the run the sentence cites, `r-20261020T053852305957`, whose probe records only the whole-page totals 895,709 B warm and 1,167,379 B cold

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_render_spa_html`, `_send`, `_send_file`, `reckon sync`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_service_unit.py`, `tests/test_spa_crew_stylesheet.py` and `tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` all resolve; the two paths §17 creates are new by construction; and the anchor it states most precisely, `serve.py` at 45,479 estimated tokens, reproduces exactly by that test's own estimator.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §17's five assertions are each measurable and one negative control is declared ("drops the revision from the shell's script URLs, and the shell assertion fails"); the one assertion the described mechanism cannot satisfy is filed under reasoning below.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs "sit under the run directory and end in EXIT=", and the reader-side re-measure is §11's durable landing record, not a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `reckon/shell_assets.py` and `tests/test_the_shells_scripts_are_fetched_once.py` are named by mechanism, with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §17's compression clause cannot produce the saving the section's own premise claims, and its done-when gzip assertion cannot hold for any real asset.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §17 delivers one thing (the shell's scripts and stylesheets fetched once per revision); the `shell_assets.py` split and the token bound are constraints on that deliverable, not a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the head's `plan-section-depends-on` gives `#s11` a predecessor of `#s17` and s17 itself needs none: §13, §14 and §16, which §17 builds on, are all declared done, so no edge is missing and none points at the wrong node.
